item: R730: per-language person/organisation rejects (function words, Swedish demonyms, Finnish place genitives, Nordic event abbreviations); text_processor keeps script marks
refs: R730; field test 2026-11-14 rows 62 and 70; WWW_INDEXER_VERSION 2
key_paths: src/timemap/entextract.py; src/timemap/whostore.py; src/analytics/reindex_parallel.py; src/analytics/engine_identity.py; src/services/text_processor.py; tests/test_entextract_r730.py
summary: extract_entities takes the article's language (whostore, the pooled re-index, the reader, the perception harness pass it). Tested languages only (sv fi da nb nn no de en fr; none without a language): a person candidate is rejected when it spans a line break, when a token is in a HAND-CURATED closed-class list for the language (articles, prepositions, conjunctions, pronouns, auxiliaries; name particles and words that are names, e.g. Till Can Son Eli He Han Le, left out; the stopwords-iso grammar list was tried first and dropped Thomas Mann, Sebastian Kurz, Fritz Lang, Dag Hammarskjold), a Swedish definite demonym (-bon/-borna), or a Finnish -n/-en genitive of a FINNISH city of 20,000+ in the gazetteer, reading long vowels and the common consonant gradations (Helsingin, Turun, Lahden, Seinäjoen; Simon/Simo and Helen/Hel stay names); a candidate across a line break is dropped whole (trimming it to its first word was tried and kept headline verbs such as 'President Warns'); VM/EM/OS/SM/NM/DM are never organisations in the Nordic languages. Sample (9 languages, 18 real people, 7 field-shaped junk names): junk 7 -> 0, real names kept unchanged. The www inputs digest now holds the article's language (entities read it), and a restore whose language resolution moves re-extracts the www half too. The grammar stoplists joined the www data digest (WWW_SHARED_DATA_GLOBS) without leaving the keyword one. Not addressed: German and English capitalised role nouns ('Minister Olaf', 'Prime Minister') still read as people. The /api/keywords text processor now keeps script combining marks (Mn/Mc), never the Latin and symbol diacritic blocks, enclosing marks or variation selectors, so a keycap emoji is no keyword (the Latin decomposition it always did is unchanged).
